headline: A US envoy says a strike on Iran could come "absolutely" this weekend, France arrests nearly 1,000 protesters, and India's voter-roll row is back on Delhi's streets
standfirst: The US blockade of Iranian ports has passed 100 days and Brent sits near 113 dollars, while the Houthis claim seven strikes on Saudi targets in one day. Israel votes on Tuesday with neither bloc at a majority. In India, the Jio Platforms IPO closed 22 times subscribed, the JD(U) expelled Anant Singh, and a Bay of Bengal system is forecast to become a cyclone. On Hacker News, Local Wikipedia holds the top spot for a second day and an Apollo note on AI's missing payoff draws the most comments.
notes: First Phoenix run of 25 October. No browser tool was connected, so the owner's X feed was not read; one web search for trending tech and AI stood in for it and found nothing newer than 23 October.

Ground News: the home page showed only the Daily Briefing card (8 stories, 1,303 articles, led by the DOJ suit over the Alaska Senate race); its Latest News list did not render. /interest/world returned an empty page again. /interest/india was read in full: JD(U) expels Anant Singh (12 sources), Defence Secretary tenure extended (11), Jaishankar meets Aliyev in Baku (8), and an India-Russia trade Blindspot (12 sources, only 17% left).

Pages that could not be read: stealmybitcoin.com (timed out twice), Roku's developer blog (rendered empty), ANI's Anant Singh report and Business Standard's cyclone report (both HTTP 403). Those cards use other outlets or search snippets.

Not carried: a school-assembly digest said Ashoke Sen became the first Indian to win the Oskar Klein Medal and that the Jio IPO drew over 1 crore applications, a world first. Searches confirmed neither. The digest's claim of heavy rain in West Bengal from 28 October also does not match current forecasts, which point at Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
The Mac went to sleep during the first page-reading pass, which ended early; it was rerun as two smaller passes with caffeinate keeping the machine awake.

sections.title: Tech
sections.blurb: The Hacker News front page and the tech press. The X feed was not reachable this run.

stories.title: Local Wikipedia, "Wikipedia, but only for things a half hour walk from you", tops Hacker News for a second day
stories.summary: Ed Jefferson's small site lists Wikipedia articles near a location you give it. It has 1,554 points, the day's maximum and up from 1,311 yesterday.
stories.heat: HN 1,554 pts (day's max), 244 comments · second day on the front page · single-platform story
detail: Local Wikipedia is a one-page interface by Ed Jefferson: you search for a place and it shows a "Nearby" list of Wikipedia articles within roughly a 30-minute walk. The page says the site "has no affiliation with the actual Wikipedia".

It is the top item on the Hacker News front page for the second day running, with 1,554 points and 244 comments this morning against 1,311 points in yesterday's run. The attention is almost entirely on HN; no major outlet has written about it.

stories.title: Apollo's chief economist: "No signs of AI payoff outside the tech sector"
stories.summary: Torsten Slok shows revenue per worker and margins rising for the Magnificent 7 but flat for the other 493 S&P companies. It is the most-discussed thread on HN today, with 504 comments.
stories.heat: HN 502 pts, 504 comments (most comments on the front page) · lands the same week Meta fell on AI-spending fears
detail: In a Daily Spark note dated 24 October 2026, Apollo partner and chief economist Torsten Slok argues that AI has produced no visible financial payoff for US companies outside tech. Revenue per worker is rising for the Magnificent 7 and flat for the "S&P 493", and profit margins split the same way.
Slok also finds no sign yet that AI is lifting productivity growth. His charts cite Bloomberg, Macrobond, the San Francisco Fed, the BLS and Ramp's AI Index.
He concludes that "the AI story will be decided in the S&P 493, not the Mag 7", and that companies outside tech may start to see token spending "as a cost center that weighs on margins".
The thread has 504 comments, the most on today's front page. It arrives as Yahoo Finance reports Meta's stock closed Friday lower on continuing AI-spending fears.

stories.title: Node2Shell becomes HTTP2Shell: the Brotli decoder flaw reaches Python, and common HTTP clients load it automatically
stories.summary: CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in Google's Brotli decoder rated 9.2, affects Brotli 1.0.3 to 1.2.0. Aikido says requests and httpx pull it in and audit tools do not flag it yet.
stories.heat: HN 282 pts, 140 comments · Node.js and Python advisories · still widening (post updated 24 Oct)
detail: Aikido Security's post (23 October, updated 24 October) covers CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Google Brotli decoder affecting versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0. It carries a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2, Critical.

Node.js disclosed it on 21 or 22 October as "node2shell" (the post gives both dates) and Python followed a day later. Aikido says OpenAI found the flaw in February; the root cause was fixed in Brotli's source but not recognised as a security issue until now.
Affected Python packages are Brotli 1.2.0 and earlier and brotlicffi 1.2.0.x; the fixes are Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0. Node.js fixes are 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1.

Aikido says HTTP clients such as requests and httpx load these packages automatically when installed, and that pip-audit, Dependabot and Safety do not yet flag the vulnerable versions. Brotli has 82.8 million monthly downloads on PyPI.

stories.title: OpenAI aims for a 30 billion dollar round at a 1.25 trillion dollar valuation, as Meta closes the week lower on AI-spending fears
stories.summary: Yahoo Finance reports the round size; CNBC reported on Friday that UAE investors would lead it. Meta's Friday fall is the market side of the same debate.
stories.heat: Yahoo Finance and CNBC · carried from yesterday, still being reported · no HN thread in the top 30
detail: Yahoo Finance reports OpenAI is aiming for a new 30 billion dollar funding round at a 1.25 trillion dollar valuation. CNBC reported on 23 October that investors from the UAE are expected to lead it.
Yahoo Finance also reports Meta's stock closed Friday down as fears about AI spending continued to weigh on the market, the same question the Apollo note on HN raises from the earnings side.

stories.title: Show HN: Steal My Bitcoin, an open challenge to take coins from a published wallet
stories.summary: The third-highest item on HN with 423 points and 259 comments. The site timed out twice when read, so this card rests on the HN thread only.
stories.heat: HN 423 pts, 259 comments · one source, the site itself was unreachable
detail: Steal My Bitcoin is a Show HN post that sits third on the front page with 423 points and 259 comments. The site timed out on two attempts this morning, so its terms, the amount at stake and how the wallet is secured could not be checked. Treat the description as the HN title only.

stories.title: Physicists trap a single antimatter particle for a month, opening a precise test of matter against antimatter
stories.summary: Gerald Gabrielse's Northwestern team held one positron for a month at 0.3 degrees above absolute zero. They now plan to compare its magnetic moment with the electron's.
stories.heat: HN 285 pts, 80 comments · Scientific American, Physical Review Letters
detail: Scientific American (Clara Moskowitz, 21 October) reports that physicists led by Gerald Gabrielse of Northwestern University trapped a single positron for a month, and that the trap could hold it indefinitely. The result is in Physical Review Letters.
The positrons come from sodium-22, slowed in a sliver of cold tungsten and held in a vacuum at "three tenths of a degree Celsius above absolute zero".

The team plans to measure the positron's magnetic moment and compare it with the electron's, which they have measured to one part in 10 trillion. Any difference could help explain why the universe is made of matter rather than antimatter.

stories.title: Goose, a memory-safe systems language with no heap allocator or garbage collector, "produced almost entirely with AI"
stories.summary: Wouter van Oortmerssen's new language claims 1.13 times the speed of the best safe Rust over 16 benchmarks. The figures are the author's own.
stories.heat: HN 266 pts, 178 comments · author's own page, benchmarks not independently checked
detail: Goose is described on its page as "a memory-safe systems language with no heap allocator, garbage collector, or lifetime annotations". Its author is Wouter van Oortmerssen, and the page says the roughly 30,000-line C++ repository was "produced almost entirely with AI", crediting Claude Fable as the implementer. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.

The benchmark table gives a geometric mean over 16 benchmarks of 3.51 times idiomatic C++, 1.24 times hand-optimised C++, 1.13 times the best safe Rust, and 1.95 times less peak memory. The introduction says 3.3 times idiomatic C++, which does not match the table.

stories.title: America has lost more than 200,000 jobs in media, film and the arts in four years. How much is AI?
stories.summary: Joseph Politano's Apricitas piece finds film and sound recording lost nearly a third of their jobs. He says AI is hard to separate from consolidation and offshoring.
stories.heat: HN 204 pts, 179 comments · Apricitas Economics, published 27 Sep, resurfaced today
detail: Apricitas Economics (Joseph Politano, 27 September 2026) counts more than 200,000 jobs lost in US creative industries over four years, about 50,000 of them in the last year. Movie and sound recording lost more than 100,000, nearly a third of the sector, and written publishing more than 70,000.

Politano says only the 2001 and 2008 recessions look similar. About 32% of arts, entertainment and recreation workers use generative AI against a 62% average across industries, and he argues AI's effect is hard to separate from consolidation, offshoring and social media.

stories.title: Dan Luu: "We should be more ambitious with the software we build"
stories.summary: Luu argues AI tools make once-too-costly projects practical, citing a Postgres rewrite that found real Postgres bugs and a one-dollar zstd implementation.
stories.heat: HN 216 pts, 176 comments
detail: Dan Luu argues builders can now attempt projects that used to cost too much. He cites Michael Malis's pgrust, a Postgres rewrite that uncovered real Postgres bugs, though Malis warns it is not ready as a primary production database.

Luu's own examples include a regex engine, a ripgrep fork and an Azul game AI built in about 20 hours, and he reports a zstd implementation by GPT-6 Astra that passes all registered tests more than 99% of the time for about 1 dollar. An appendix carries Yossi Kreinin's counterargument that most people should be less ambitious.

stories.title: Mathematicians launch a community hub on Terry Tao's blog to revise OpenAI's math write-ups
stories.summary: The oai-math-revised project invites students and professors to rewrite OpenAI's published proofs, which its authors say can be hard to follow and under-cited. Commenters ask why unpaid academics should do it.
stories.heat: HN 37 pts, 28 comments · Tao's blog · early, still building
detail: A guest post on Terry Tao's blog dated 24 October, by Abhinav Nellore, Johannes Schmitt, Soledad Villar and Rachel Ward, introduces oai-math-revised on GitHub to revise OpenAI's math write-ups, which the authors say "can be difficult to understand and can have incomplete citations". Comment-thread critics argue the work benefits a for-profit company and could become training data; one asks, "Why is it our job to revise OpenAI's manuscripts?"

stories.title: Also: Roku moves its developer repos from GitHub to GitLab, FreeDNS, how close pure FP can get to C, and Xbox's first COO is out
stories.summary: Smaller items, one line each.
stories.heat: HN 268 pts and 183 comments (Roku), 261 pts (FreeDNS), 258 pts (FP vs C), 196 pts (gpu-unlock), 164 pts (AI language) · The Verge · GeekWire
detail: Roku says its developer repositories are moving from GitHub to GitLab (268 points, 183 comments; the blog post rendered empty, so the details are the HN title only). Also on HN: FreeDNS (261 points), Richard Feldman on how close pure functional programming can get to C (258), gpu-unlock for FP and BF16 issue rates on RTX 3000 cards (196), and an arXiv paper on why AI-generated language is hard to understand (164).

The Verge reports Xbox's first chief operating officer is out after a few months, and GeekWire reports Amazon has ended its six-year legal fight with former AWS managers over alleged data-centre kickbacks.

sections.title: Geopolitics
sections.blurb: Ground News Daily Briefing (the World page was empty), Iran International, CBS News and AP, Xinhua, Al Jazeera, Haaretz and Ukrinform.

stories.title: US envoy Tom Barrack says a strike on Iran could come "absolutely" this weekend, as the blockade passes 100 days and Brent nears 113 dollars
stories.summary: The NYT reports US and Israeli planners have a short, intense campaign ready for after the 3 November midterms. Iran repeats that it would reopen Hormuz within seven days if the blockade ends.
stories.heat: Iran International, CBS live blog, Dawn live, NYT via Iran International · oil up about 4% · still escalating
detail: Iran International (analysis, 24 October) reports that Tom Barrack, the US ambassador to Turkey, said on Friday a US strike on Iran could "absolutely" come this weekend. It cites the New York Times as reporting that US and Israeli planners have drawn up a short, intensive campaign for after the 3 November midterms, aimed at Iran's missile and drone arsenal, nuclear sites and energy infrastructure.

CENTCOM marked 100 days of the reinstated blockade on 22 October and says it has stopped 25 billion dollars of Iranian crude exports, CBS reports. The blockade was reimposed on 14 July after the Islamabad memorandum collapsed over who controls transit.

The IRGC says it attacked four vessels using a route Tehran rejects, and Brent rose about 4% to 112 to 113 dollars a barrel. Trump accused Iran of inventing ship-strike and mine reports to push up oil prices before the midterms; neither claim has been independently confirmed.

Iran's ambassador to Pakistan told Dawn that Tehran had offered, through Islamabad, to reopen the strait if Washington lifted the blockade. Iran International says the standing offer is reopening within seven days in exchange for ending the blockade, easing oil sanctions and releasing frozen assets. US Ambassador Mike Waltz told the Financial Times the blockade can stay in place for the foreseeable future.

stories.title: Houthis claim seven missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil sites and a base in one day; coalition airstrikes hit Sanaa province
stories.summary: Targets named include Riyadh, Yanbu, Rabigh, Dammam, Najran and Khamis Mushait, and the Houthis say they hit the East-West Pipeline. Saudi forces confirm interceptions but not pipeline damage.
stories.heat: Xinhua, Al Jazeera, Dawn, PBS, CBS · follows the Dammam airport deaths · still escalating
detail: Xinhua (published 25 October) reports the Houthis said they launched seven missile and drone attacks on 24 October on airports, oil facilities and a military base in Riyadh, Yanbu, Rabigh, Dammam, Najran and Khamis Mushait. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted several missiles and a drone.

The Houthis say they struck the East-West Pipeline and Aramco facilities in Yanbu and Rabigh. Dawn reports Saudi forces intercepted two missiles aimed at Yanbu and Taif. Damage to the pipeline has not been verified; CBS reports Aramco says the pipeline's capacity has been raised from 2 million to 7 million barrels a day.
Houthi-run al-Masirah TV said coalition airstrikes on housing in Sanaa province's Hamdan district killed eight people and wounded more than 10, Xinhua reports. The figure is from one side only.

This follows the 22 October strike on Dammam's King Fahd airport, which Al Jazeera and CBS say killed two people. The US State Department has updated its Middle East travel advisories, and Indian carriers suspended Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam flights until at least 24 October.

stories.title: Israel's final polls before Tuesday's vote give neither bloc a majority; thousands rally in Hostages Square for an October 7 inquiry
stories.summary: Channel 12 puts Eisenkot's Yashar first with 23 seats to Likud's 21; Maariv gives the opposition 54 to the coalition's 48. The West Bank will be closed on election day.
stories.heat: Haaretz live, Jerusalem Post, Al Jazeera, Fortune, Turkiye Today · vote on 27 Oct, building
detail: The last polls before Tuesday's election were published on 24 October. Haaretz reports Channel 12 projects Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar as the largest party with 23 seats and Likud at 21, with the anti-Netanyahu bloc at 70 (56 Zionist "change bloc" seats and 14 Arab party seats) against 50 for the coalition. Maariv, per the Jerusalem Post, gives the opposition 54 and the coalition 48.
Neither count gives the change bloc 61 without Arab parties, so coalition-building after the vote is likely to be slow.

Al Jazeera reports thousands rallied in Tel Aviv's Hostages Square on Saturday. The October Council, a group of hostage families, demanded an independent state commission of inquiry into 7 October; Eisenkot and Yair Golan attended. The government has offered only a "political" commission, half of it government-appointed, which the opposition says it will boycott.
The government approved a general closure of the West Bank for election day: no entry or exit for Palestinian workers and all land crossings shut.

stories.title: About 410,000 march across France and nearly 1,000 are arrested as clashes break out in Paris and other cities
stories.summary: Police counted 110,000 in Paris, where the march ended with attacks on police and tear gas. Unions put the national turnout at 800,000; the next round is set for 31 October.
stories.heat: CBS/AP, CNN live, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Connexion · peaked Saturday, next date 31 Oct
detail: Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said nearly 1,000 people were arrested nationwide on Saturday 24 October, CBS and AP report. The Interior Ministry put turnout at about 410,000 across roughly 298 protests; union organisers said 800,000.

In Paris, police counted 110,000 marchers and unions 250,000 on the route from Porte d'Italie to Porte de Vincennes. CNN reports the march ended with several thousand people attacking police, who used tear gas and water cannon; the Paris prosecutor reported 64 arrests in the city.

Marches were banned in Lyon, Marseille and Nice, and police numbers were 20% higher than on 17 October. In Nice, 11 people were arrested after far-right extremists fought demonstrators. Thousands also marched in Orleans against Marine Le Pen's National Rally congress there.

The protests centre on the cost of living and the education system. The next Yellow Vest round is set for 31 October. CBS also notes 371 people detained at protests in Italy and 500 extra soldiers sent to Milan.

stories.title: Russia fires about 30 ballistic missiles at Ukraine's energy grid as both sides plan November talks in the UAE
stories.summary: Strikes killed people in Kharkiv and Dnipropetrovsk regions. Al Jazeera reports a localised ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump, and Romania blames Russia for a drone that sank a ship in the Black Sea.
stories.heat: Ukrinform, Al Jazeera · daily strikes continue · talks date set, not yet held
detail: Al Jazeera reports Russia fired about 30 ballistic missiles overnight at Ukraine's energy infrastructure, injuring six people in Kyiv. Ukrinform's 23 to 25 October entries include a drone strike on Kharkiv that killed one and injured three, a strike on Synelnykove in Dnipropetrovsk region that killed three and injured eight, and a power cut in a Vinnytsia district after an energy facility was hit. Ukrainian officials counted 181 clashes in a day, heaviest on the Kostiantynivka axis.

Russia and Ukraine say talks with the US are planned for November in the UAE, after Putin signalled willingness following a Witkoff visit. Al Jazeera also reports a localised ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump, which Trump praised on 24 October; its scope is not clear and strikes continued.
Romania blamed Russia after a drone sank a ship in the Black Sea. Zelensky says Starlink and Starshield are back to earlier speeds, and Trump said Elon Musk had restored access.

stories.title: Also: the DOJ sues to block Alaska's Senate certification over a same-name candidate, Bulgaria votes for president, and China's Fifth Plenum
stories.summary: Smaller items, one line each.
stories.heat: Ground News Daily Briefing (8 stories, 1,303 articles) · Al Jazeera · RANE Worldview
detail: Ground News leads its Daily Briefing with a federal lawsuit, filed Thursday, claiming a retired teacher named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. entered Alaska's Senate race to confuse voters and draw support from the Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan; the DOJ seeks to block certification. The same card lists ICE detention without hearings upheld, Treasury targeting Chinese AI investments, and Trump denying interference in Ukraine's Starlink.

Al Jazeera reports Bulgarians vote in a presidential election on 25 October. RANE Worldview lists China's Fifth Plenum, where Xi Jinping gathers senior cadres with a focus on discipline, and Houthi forces encircling Taiz in Yemen.

sections.title: India
sections.blurb: Ground News /interest/india, TIME, Onmanorama, HDFC Sky, IANS, ANI-sourced reports and national outlets. Single-source items are flagged unverified.

stories.title: Voter-roll protests return to Delhi: marchers head for the Election Commission and 273 paramilitary companies stay deployed until 31 October
stories.summary: Protesters say the Special Intensive Revision has removed more than 130 million names; the Election Commission says it removes only dead, moved and untraceable voters. Phase two starts in 12 states and UTs on 4 November.
stories.heat: TIME opinion, Onmanorama, Reuters via Express Tribune, Democracy Now · national row for weeks · next phase 4 Nov
detail: Onmanorama reports that on 23 October the Delhi Coordination Committee of People Against SIR marched towards Election Commission headquarters over alleged voter deletions. The Union Home Ministry extended the deployment of 273 CAPF companies in Delhi until 31 October, citing the risk of flash protests, and traffic was diverted around Connaught Place, Parliament Street and Jantar Mantar.

Protesters say the Special Intensive Revision has removed more than 130 million names from the rolls. That total comes from protesters and critics; no official figure confirming it was found. TIME's opinion piece by Asim Ali (24 October) cites a SABAR Institute study finding 9.08 million voters removed from West Bengal's rolls, and says this is the first time the process has put the burden of proving eligibility on citizens.

The Election Commission says the exercise removes only dead, relocated and untraceable people. Critics say deletions fall hardest on Muslims and other minorities, which the BJP denies. Protesters are demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, and Amit Shah has attacked Rahul Gandhi over his "vote theft" claims.
Punjab's assembly has passed a resolution calling for an independent investigation. The Election Commission says phase two of the SIR will run in 12 states and Union Territories from 4 November.

stories.title: Jio Platforms IPO closes about 22 times subscribed, with institutions bidding 70 times; listing is due on 28 October
stories.summary: The roughly 30,213 crore rupee fresh issue drew 70.55 times on the QIB book and 2.72 times from retail. Allotment is on 26 October.
stories.heat: Business Standard, HDFC Sky, Chittorgarh, IIFL · India's biggest issue · allotment Monday, listing Wednesday
detail: HDFC Sky reports the Jio Platforms IPO was subscribed 22.19 times overall by 7 pm IST on 23 October, the final day. Chittorgarh's live page showed 21.36 times at 7.28 pm, so the final figure should be checked against NSE and BSE data.

Qualified institutional buyers bid 70.55 times their portion, non-institutional investors 14.00 times and retail investors 2.72 times. Business Standard reported the book was fully covered within 100 minutes of opening on 21 October.
The issue is a fresh issue of 27 crore shares priced at 1,065 to 1,119 rupees, about 30,213 crore rupees at the top of the band.

Allotment is due on 26 October, refunds and demat credit on 27 October, and a tentative listing on the BSE and NSE on 28 October. A digest's claim that the IPO drew over 1 crore applications, a global first, could not be confirmed.

stories.title: JD(U) expels Mokama MLA Anant Singh and his wife Neelam Devi for six years and asks the Speaker to disqualify him
stories.summary: The party cites derogatory language about its leadership and his backing of a rival in the Patna Graduates' council poll. Days earlier he claimed to have got "nine people murdered".
stories.heat: Ground News 12 sources (67% right) · ANI, Oneindia, Punjab Kesari, NewsMill · Bihar's top political story
detail: The Janata Dal (United) on Saturday 24 October expelled Mokama MLA Anant Kumar Singh and his wife, former MLA Neelam Devi, for six years over anti-party activities, according to ANI-sourced reports carried by Punjab Kesari and NewsMill. The party asked the Bihar Assembly Speaker to act against his membership under the Tenth Schedule, the anti-defection law.

The order cites persistent disregard for party directives, derogatory language about the top leadership and actions against the party's candidate. The dispute centres on the Patna Graduates' Legislative Council poll, where Singh backed a Jan Suraaj-linked candidate against JD(U) nominee Neeraj Kumar; Free Press Journal reported on 4 October that he had vowed to defeat Kumar.

Days before the expulsion Singh reportedly claimed he had got "nine people murdered", which drew attacks from the RJD; Oneindia ties the expulsion to that remark, while other outlets cite only the council-poll dispute. Singh says the statement has been refuted. He won Mokama in November 2025 while in custody and was bailed in March 2026.

stories.title: Bay of Bengal system forecast to become a cyclonic storm by 26 October and head for the north Andhra and south Odisha coast around 28 October
stories.summary: Some reports say it could become a very severe cyclonic storm by 27 October. IMD's own bulletin was not read, and forecasts differ on strength.
stories.heat: Business Standard, Daily Jagran, Asianet Newsable, Indian Opinion · forecast stage, building
detail: Business Standard's 24 October headline says the Bay of Bengal system is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm by 26 October (the article itself returned HTTP 403). Daily Jagran reports the IMD expects the depression to become a very severe cyclonic storm by 27 October and warns of heavy rain in Andhra Pradesh.

Reports put the system near the north Andhra Pradesh coast on the morning of 28 October, with a likely landfall between north Andhra and south Odisha. A digest said President Murmu's visit had been postponed and that coastal West Bengal would get heavy rain from 28 October; current forecasts do not name West Bengal, so check IMD bulletins at mausam.imd.gov.in.

stories.title: Modi watches the IAF's "Wings over Ganges" display at Namo Ghat and opens the RBI's new data centre in Bhubaneswar today
stories.summary: The aerial display marks the Air Force's 94th anniversary. The RBI's Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute is certified Tier IV.
stories.heat: IANS via Siasat · today's schedule · one wire report
detail: IANS (via Siasat, 25 October) reports Modi will open a garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi at about 11 am, then attend the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat as chief guest, marking the IAF's 94th anniversary under the theme "Wings over Ganges".
He then travels to Bhubaneswar to inaugurate the RBI's Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute, which IANS says is certified to Uptime Institute Tier IV.

stories.title: India's flash composite PMI rises to a four-month high of 56.7, but services hiring stalls for the first time in nine months
stories.summary: Services rose to 56.2 and manufacturing slipped to 54.9. Export orders grew at the fastest pace in six months.
stories.heat: NationPath India (one outlet read) · HSBC flash data released 24 Oct
detail: NationPath India reports the HSBC Flash India Composite PMI rose to 56.7 in October from 55.9 in September. The services flash index rose to 56.2 from 55.2 while manufacturing slipped to 54.9 from 55.1.

Export orders grew at their fastest pace in six months and input-cost inflation eased to its lowest in almost a year, but services employment was unchanged, ending nine months of hiring growth. Only one outlet's account was read, so the card is marked unverified.

stories.title: India and Russia restate a 100 billion dollar trade goal for 2030; Ground News flags it as a right-leaning Blindspot
stories.summary: Twelve sources carry the Modi and Putin push, only 17% of them on the left. The goal itself dates from July 2024.
stories.heat: Ground News 12 sources, Blindspot (only 17% left) · Outlook, Anadolu
detail: Ground News lists the India-Russia push for 100 billion dollars of trade by 2030 as a Blindspot, covered by 12 sources with only 17% on the left. The target was first set in July 2024, and Modi said in December 2025 it could be met early. Trade was 68.7 billion dollars in the last financial year by one count and is heavily in Russia's favour. No new October announcement was found behind the current coverage.

stories.title: Also: Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh's term reportedly extended by a year, Jaishankar meets Aliyev in Baku, and Indian airlines' Saudi pause
stories.summary: Smaller items, one line each.
stories.heat: Ground News 11 sources (Defence Secretary), 8 sources (Jaishankar) · Indian Masterminds · Indian Opinion
detail: Ground News lists "Centre extends Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh's tenure by one year" with 11 sources; his term was due to end on 31 October, and Indian Masterminds reported only speculation as of 21 October. No government order was found. Ground News also lists Jaishankar meeting Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev in Baku (8 sources); searches found only India's new ambassador presenting credentials to Aliyev on 16 October, so details are thin.

Air India, Air India Express, IndiGo and Akasa Air suspended flights to Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam until at least 24 October after the Houthi attacks on Saudi airports; check with the airline for the current status.
